old: For the EU launch, customer exports must be encrypted with the customer-specific KMS key.
new: All customer exports must use the platform KMS key unless a contract requires a customer-specific key.
note: The newer general rule does not cancel the EU contractual requirement; the special case remains valid.

old: During the mobile-app migration, the billing service may temporarily read from the legacy database.
new: Services participating in the migration should read from the new database only.
note: The general migration rule can coexist with the earlier temporary exception for billing.

old: For the September release, Android builds are signed with the release signing key stored in Vault.
new: All production builds must use signing keys stored in the central HSM.
note: The general HSM policy does not explicitly cancel the September Android release procedure, so both can be valid during that release.

old: All pull requests require two approvals before merging into the default branch.
new: The documentation team may merge its own documentation pull requests with one approval.
note: The second decision creates a team-specific exception rather than changing the general approval requirement.

old: Production database access requires approval from the on-call engineering manager.
new: For the payments service, production database access requires approval from the payments service owner.
note: The payments service has a narrower approval path while the general production-access rule can still apply elsewhere.

old: Customer support tickets containing personal data must be deleted after 90 days.
new: Tickets from enterprise customers under a contractual retention agreement must be retained for the period specified in that agreement.
note: The enterprise contractual requirement is a specific exception and does not necessarily invalidate the general retention rule.

old: The analytics team stores application logs in the us-east-1 S3 bucket.
new: The security team stores audit logs in the eu-west-1 S3 bucket.
note: The sentences use similar storage terminology but concern different teams and different log systems.

old: The checkout service uses Redis for session storage.
new: The recommendation service uses Redis for feature-cache storage.
note: Both decisions mention Redis, but they concern different services and different purposes.

old: The staging environment sends email through MailHog.
new: The development environment sends email through MailHog.
note: The same tool is selected for two different environments, so both decisions can hold simultaneously.

old: The India support team starts its daily handoff at 5:30 PM IST.
new: The US support team starts its daily handoff at 5:30 PM IST.
note: The time and topic are similar, but the decisions concern different teams.

old: We will use PostgreSQL for the reporting service because the queries need relational joins.
new: We will use PostgreSQL for the reporting service. The schema will keep customer, invoice, and subscription data in separate tables so joins remain straightforward.
note: The later decision preserves the same database choice and adds implementation detail.

old: The incident channel is created by the on-call engineer.
new: The incident channel is created by the on-call engineer, and the incident commander owns the channel description.
note: The original channel-creation decision remains unchanged; the later text adds an owner for another detail.

old: Recruiter screens are scheduled for 30 minutes.
new: Recruiter screens are scheduled for 30 minutes so candidates receive a consistent initial conversation.
note: The duration is identical and the added sentence only explains the reason.

old: The weekly product review is on Thursday at 4 PM.
new: The weekly product review is on Thursday at 4 PM. Maya owns the agenda and sends it the morning before the meeting.
note: The meeting schedule is preserved and the later decision adds ownership detail.

old: We will keep feature flags in LaunchDarkly and require a ticket for production changes.
new: We will keep feature flags in LaunchDarkly and require a ticket for production changes. The platform team owns the LaunchDarkly project.
note: Both original decisions remain intact; only an ownership detail is added.

old: The API has a 30-second timeout, retries failed requests twice, and logs request IDs.
new: The API has a 30-second timeout, retries failed requests three times, and logs request IDs.
note: The same three-part configuration is being decided, and the retry count is the only conflicting part.

old: Support escalations go to the platform team, receive a response within four hours, and are tracked in Jira.
new: Support escalations go to the platform team, receive a response within eight hours, and are tracked in Jira.
note: The same escalation policy is being defined, with only the response target differing.

old: The hiring process has a recruiter screen, one coding interview, and one system-design interview.
new: The hiring process has a recruiter screen, one coding interview, and two system-design interviews.
note: The later decision defines the same interview process while changing one component.

old: Invoices are generated on the first business day of each month.
new: Invoices are generated on the third business day of each month.
note: Both decisions answer the same scheduling question for invoice generation, with different dates.

old: The design system uses 8px spacing increments, Inter for UI text, and rounded buttons.
new: The design system uses 8px spacing increments, Inter for UI text, and square buttons.
note: The same three design choices are addressed and the button-shape decision conflicts.

old: All production deployments require a successful integration-test suite and a manual approval.
new: Production deployments require a successful integration-test suite and a manual approval from the release manager.
note: The later decision contains the original requirements and adds the identity of the approver.

old: The dashboard refreshes every 60 seconds.
new: The dashboard refreshes every 30 seconds during the launch week; after launch week, it follows the standard 60-second interval.
note: The later decision introduces a temporary launch-week behavior while explicitly retaining the permanent 60-second rule.

old: Customer-facing API rate limits are 100 requests per minute per account.
new: For the Black Friday launch weekend, customer-facing API rate limits are 250 requests per minute per account.
note: The second decision is explicitly limited to a temporary event and does not establish a permanent rate limit.

old: All finance reports are generated from the production warehouse.
new: During the quarter-end close, finance reports may be generated from the replicated warehouse if the production warehouse is under maintenance.
note: The later decision defines a narrow temporary contingency without removing the permanent source.

old: The incident review happens every Monday at 10 AM.
new: The incident review happens every Monday at 10 AM, except during the annual company shutdown when it is skipped.
note: The general schedule remains the same and the later text adds a narrow exception.

old: New employees receive laptops before their first working day.
new: For the January office move, new employees starting that week collect laptops from IT on their first working day.
note: The later decision describes a one-off operational arrangement rather than a permanent hiring policy.

old: The service uses JSON for its public API responses.
new: The service uses Protocol Buffers for its public API responses.
note: Both decisions specify the representation for the same public API, so the formats conflict.

old: Engineering interviews are conducted remotely.
new: Engineering interviews are conducted in person at the Bengaluru office.
note: Both decisions specify the interview setting for the same process.

old: The team stores uploaded images in S3.
new: The team stores uploaded images in Azure Blob Storage.
note: The same storage decision for uploaded images has two incompatible destinations.

old: Support refunds up to $50 without manager approval.
new: Support refunds up to $100 without manager approval.
note: Both statements define the same approval threshold for support refunds.

old: The team uses GitHub Actions for CI.
new: The team uses GitLab CI for CI.
note: The same CI system choice is being defined with incompatible tools.

old: Password reset links expire after one hour.
new: Password reset links expire after 15 minutes.
note: Both decisions define the expiration period for the same password-reset links.

old: The mobile app asks for notification permission during onboarding.
new: The mobile app asks for notification permission after the user creates their first project.
note: Both statements specify when the same permission prompt appears in the same app.

old: Marketing owns the company LinkedIn page.
new: The employer-branding team owns the company LinkedIn page.
note: The two statements assign ownership of the same account to different teams.

old: All security incidents are reported in the security channel.
new: The payments team reports payment-processing incidents in the payments incident channel.
note: The later statement can define a service-specific reporting path without necessarily eliminating the broader security reporting requirement.

old: Design reviews happen in Figma comments.
new: Accessibility reviews happen in GitHub pull requests.
note: The decisions concern different review types and can both be followed.

old: The backend team deploys on Tuesday and Thursday.
new: The data team deploys on Wednesday and Friday.
note: The schedules concern different teams and do not conflict.

old: Candidates for engineering roles complete a coding exercise before the technical interview.
new: Candidates for product-design roles complete a portfolio review before the design interview.
note: Both are hiring-process decisions but apply to different roles.

old: The API gateway blocks requests missing an authorization header.
new: The health-check endpoint accepts requests without an authorization header.
note: The second statement is about a specific endpoint and can coexist with the general gateway rule.

old: Engineering uses Slack for incident communication.
new: The customer-success team uses Microsoft Teams for incident communication.
note: The communication choices apply to different teams, so similar wording does not imply a conflict.

old: All database migrations require a maintenance window.
new: The user-profile migration will run online without a maintenance window because its schema change is backward compatible.
note: The user-profile migration is a concrete exception to the general policy.

old: The support team responds to priority-two tickets within eight business hours.
new: Priority-two tickets from enterprise customers receive a response within four business hours.
note: The enterprise SLA can be a customer-specific exception while the eight-hour rule remains applicable to other priority-two tickets.

old: The search index is rebuilt every Sunday night.
new: The search index is rebuilt every Sunday night. The data platform team owns the job and receives an alert if it fails.
note: The schedule is unchanged and the later text adds operational ownership and monitoring detail.

old: Expense approvals above $5,000 require finance review.
new: Expense approvals above $5,000 require finance review, with the CFO handling requests above $25,000.
note: The later policy retains the original threshold and adds a higher-level approval requirement.

old: The data export job runs every night at midnight.
new: The data export job runs every night at midnight in UTC.
note: The later sentence clarifies the timezone without changing the intended schedule.

old: The team will not hold the weekly planning meeting on October 2 because the office is closed.
new: Weekly planning meetings are held on Fridays at 3 PM.
note: The general recurring schedule does not cancel the previously stated one-off cancellation.

old: The billing service sends invoices at 9 AM on the first business day.
new: The billing service sends invoices at 9 AM on the first business day. For accounts with monthly closing on the last calendar day, invoices are sent the following business day.
note: The general schedule remains intact while the later text adds a specific account exception.

old: The support team uses Zendesk for customer tickets.
new: The support team uses Zendesk for customer tickets, with Priya responsible for administering the Zendesk workspace.
note: The same tool choice is preserved and only an administrator is specified.

old: The platform team owns the production Kubernetes cluster.
new: The infrastructure team owns the production Kubernetes cluster.
note: Both decisions assign ownership of the same production cluster to different teams.

old: The mobile release is scheduled for the second Tuesday of the month.
new: The mobile release is scheduled for the second Tuesday of the month unless the app-store review is still pending.
note: One reading treats the later sentence as the same schedule with a contingency; another treats the pending-review clause as a separate conditional decision that can coexist with the original schedule.

old: Customer data is retained for seven years.
new: Customer data is retained for seven years, except records covered by deletion requests are removed when the request is processed.
note: This can be read as the same retention rule with an operational detail, or as a separate deletion exception that modifies the retention policy.

old: Engineering uses the shared staging database for integration testing.
new: The payments team uses a dedicated staging database for integration testing.
note: The payments statement can be a team-specific exception to the shared database policy, but it could also be interpreted as a new organization-wide database rule if team scope was omitted.

old: Production deployments require approval from the on-call engineer.
new: Production deployments require approval from the service owner for high-risk changes.
note: The later statement may define an additional approval requirement for high-risk changes, or it may be intended to define the approval authority for all deployments; the scope is not explicit.
